summary: PASS 1 grind (2026-08-04): re-measured every non-match item against the CURRENT tree — it had moved substantially since this map was written (owner-review-1 and the search/settings passes had already fixed the rail search icon and the +new dialog; both were re-verified live and flipped to match). What remained: the message queue (built for real — client-side hold/reorder/edit/remove state plus a genuinely wired 'interrupt and deliver' backed by POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel, not a mock); the composer's ask-button mode-reset bug (one-line fix, confirmed via a failing-first test); and the shared window chrome (Layer.tsx maximize/pop-out/close, the detail-slot's Copy/Download/Maximize/Close, and the rail's collapse glyph) all still used hardcoded Unicode instead of the prototype's own SVGs. The exact paths for the LayerChrome partial (Expand/Pop out/Close) were not resolvable from the visible template source — they are decoded from the prototype's own gzip+base64 embedded resource bundle (design/prototype/Clio Session.html's line-379 manifest, key 774ac6dd-5309-49a6-896c-cfcd55579da9 -> LayerChrome.dc.html) rather than guessed, and that same decode revealed a real fact worth recording: the prototype's OWN Expand/Pop-out buttons carry no click handler at all in ANY of their five host windows (obs/files/run/bp/conf) — inert chrome even in the ground truth. This build's Expand is a real, working superset (it actually maximizes); Pop-out stays honestly disabled (no Tauri window API on web) rather than mimicking the prototype's silent no-op. Same-class sweep found and fixed one more: Modal.tsx's close button hugged a custom `header` instead of sitting at the far right (only the default title got the flex:1 that pushes it there) — affects the +new dialog, now fixed at the primitive so every future custom-header dialog gets it free. Settings' 13 placeholder pages (originally flagged here) are NOT re-verified in this pass — a parallel PASS 1 already fully built them under the dedicated 'settings' surface (docs/p5/conformance/settings.json); re-reporting them here would be stale/duplicate. Deleted the confirmed-dead CollapsiblePart.tsx (zero importers, superseded '›' glyph never reachable).

items.element: Send-while-busy message queue (reorder ↑/↓, in-place edit, remove, 'interrupt · deliver now' link)
items.proto_truth: Decoded from the prototype's own JS state (queueRows()/mainQ/mainQNow/sendTitle, design/prototype/Clio Session.html): while busy, Send enqueues instead of blocking (button title becomes 'Queue for the next step boundary', SAME arrow-up glyph). Each queued row is `#N` + text + a per-row hint ('delivers at the next step boundary' for #1, 'after message #N' otherwise), with four 20x20 icon-only controls: ↑ (mq.up, disabled at the top), ↓ (mq.down, disabled at the bottom), ✂ (mq.startEdit → an inline text input, save on blur/Enter, cancel on Escape), ✕ (mq.rm). A header row above the rows reads '{N} messages queued' (amber, uppercase) + a muted hint + a right-aligned 'interrupt and deliver' link (mainQNow/fv.deliverNow) titled 'Interrupt the current step and deliver immediately'.
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/composer/Composer.tsx (QueuedMessage type, queuedMessages/onQueueMessage/onReorderQueuedMessage/onEditQueuedMessage/onRemoveQueuedMessage/onDeliverQueuedNow props, the composer__queue tray render block) + apps/web/src/session/SessionView.tsx (queue state, onDeliverQueuedNow calling the REAL client.cancelSession() then re-sending the held messages, and a useEffect that auto-delivers the next held message as soon as `sending` clears). Locked by 5 new tests in tests/unit/composer.test.tsx ('send-while-busy message queue') and 2 end-to-end tests in tests/unit/session-view.test.tsx proving the real hold/auto-deliver and the real cancelSession() call. Verified structurally, NOT via a side-by-side screenshot — no harness setup in scripts/side-by-side.mjs exposes a busy composer to capture (disclosed gap in verification method, not in the feature).
items.backend_surface: client-owned hold/reorder/edit/remove (correct — the prototype's own queue is client state, not a wire concept); deliver-now is REAL: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel via client.cancelSession(), confirmed present on SessionOperationsClient
items.fix_hint: Known, disclosed scope limit: `busy` is this client's own send round-trip (POST -> load -> refreshPill), not the full multi-step turn the backend may still be running after that POST returns — there is no persistent live session-status subscription outside the observability panel (subscribeSessionTraceEvents only mounts when panel==='obs'). The queue behaves correctly for its own definition of busy; widening 'busy' to track the whole turn needs an always-on session-status feed, which is a distinct, larger project (touches App-level session refresh, not composer icons/buttons) — tracked as a follow-up, not silently narrowed.

items.element: Window chrome: maximize/expand button (shared by Settings, Observability, and any future windowControls surface)
items.proto_truth: Decoded from the prototype's embedded LayerChrome.dc.html partial (base64+gzip in the resource manifest, NOT visible in the plain template text — see summary): titled 'Expand' there; the detail-slot's own separate Maximize button (`detExpand`) uses the SAME path, titled 'Maximize'. Both: 12x12, `M7.2 1.5h3.3v3.3M4.8 10.5H1.5V7.2M10.5 1.5L7 5M1.5 10.5L5 7`, stroke-width 1.3. Real fact from the decode: the prototype's OWN Expand button in LayerChrome carries no onClick at all — decorative chrome even in the ground truth, on all five host kinds (obs/files/run/bp/conf).
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/kit/Icon.tsx adds an 'expand' IconName (path above). apps/web/src/kit/Layer.tsx now renders `<Icon name="expand"/>` instead of the hardcoded `⛶` (⛶) span, with `title` set to 'Expand'/'Restore'. Unlike the prototype's own inert button, this one is a REAL, working superset (toggles a genuine maximized layout state) — documented in-code as intentionally exceeding the prototype rather than matching its decorative no-op. Extended `windowControls` to FilesLayer.tsx and BlueprintWindow.tsx too (the decode shows kind="files"/kind="bp" use the identical LayerChrome partial, so they get the same chrome, not just the eye window). Locked by 3 new tests in tests/unit/kit-layer.test.tsx. Composites: screenshots/side-by-side/obs-panel.png, screenshots/side-by-side/artifacts-panel.png.
items.backend_surface: unbacked (client-only layout state, matching the prototype's own scope for this control)

items.element: Panel collapse/expand toggle icon (rail 'Collapse/Expand sessions'; detail-panel 'Collapse/Expand panel')
items.proto_truth: Two DIFFERENT instances of one shape family, both decoded from the plain template (not gzip-embedded): rail collapse/expand (tgLeft, both directions) is viewBox 0 0 14 14, rect 1.5,2.2,11x9.6 rx1.8, divider at x=5.4 (left-of-centre, marking the LEFT panel). The detail-panel's OWN collapse (tgRight, panel open) is the SAME rect shape with the divider at x=8.6 (right-of-centre); its companion 'Expand panel' (tgRight, panel collapsed to a narrow strip) is not an SVG at all — it's a literal '‹' character.
items.app_evidence: Fixed the ONE control that actually exists in the app: apps/web/src/kit/Icon.tsx's 'panel' glyph geometry was corrected from a generic 12x12/rect(1.5,1.5,9,9)/divider-at-4.5 shape to the prototype-exact 14x14/rect(1.5,2.2,11,9.6,rx1.8)/divider-at-5.4 (Rail.tsx's collapse button and Topbar.tsx's re-show-rail button both consume this, and both are the SAME tgLeft concept in the prototype, so sharing one corrected glyph is correct, not a residual gap). Locked by a new test in tests/unit/rail-conformance.test.tsx asserting the exact viewBox + divider path. NOT built this pass: the detail panel has no collapse-to-strip affordance at all — today it is only fully-open or fully-closed (via the real 'Close' button). That is a missing INTERACTION, not an icon mismatch — building it means new state (a collapsed-strip layout, the '‹' expand-strip control, DetailSlot restructuring) beyond swapping a path.
items.fix_hint: Adding the detail panel's collapse-to-strip state is a real, separate feature slice (new layout state + the tgRight-style off-center-divider icon transcribed at x=8.6 + the '‹' expand-from-strip control) — scoped out of an icon/button pass; flagged here as the residual rather than silently dropped.

items.element: Composer acceptance-mode button (the 'ask' pill that opens the ask/auto-edits/bypass/ai-review menu)
items.proto_truth: Approval mode (ask/auto-edits/bypass/ai-review) and turn mode (execute/plan) are independent wire axes; the acceptance-mode menu hangs off the 'ask' side of that row and must only ever toggle ITS OWN menu.
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/composer/Composer.tsx's approval button onClick used to unconditionally call `setMode('ask')` before toggling the menu — silently reverting a session already in 'execute'/'plan' back to 'ask' as a side effect of merely checking permissions, which then submitted as 'edit' mode instead of the user's real choice. Removed the `setMode('ask')` call; the handler now only toggles its own menu. Locked by a new failing-first test in tests/unit/composer-conformance.test.tsx ('opening the ask/permissions menu never flips the real execute/plan mode') and re-verified live via screenshots/side-by-side/execmenu-panel.png (execute stays checked with the permissions menu open).
